meta.scope: Guyana batch 3 — Administrative regions and hinterland/Indigenous geography, education and health spending/programmes, non-oil primary sectors (gold, rice, sugar, bauxite), and school-feeding / Because We Care social transfers. Completes the coastal–hinterland contrast.

candidates.title: Region 4 (Demerara-Mahaica) — coastal demographic core
candidates.description: Most populous administrative region (~40% of national population). Contains Georgetown and the densest coastal settlement.
candidates.notes: Demographic and economic core. Continuously cited as the primary concentration of population, formal activity and oil-boom construction.

candidates.title: Hinterland regions (1, 7, 8, 9)
candidates.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / Ministry of Amerindian Affairs
candidates.description: Interior regions that hold the large majority of national land area but a small share of population. Highest Indigenous population shares and historically highest poverty rates.
candidates.notes: Structural geographic contrast. ~12–13% of population on two-thirds of the land; poverty and service gaps have historically been several times higher than on the coast.

candidates.title: Amerindian / Indigenous population and villages
candidates.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / Ministry of Amerindian Affairs
candidates.description: Indigenous (Amerindian) population statistics and the system of titled and untitled villages. Fourth-largest ethnic group nationally; majority population in hinterland regions 1, 8 and 9.
candidates.notes: Core identity and territorial node. Continuously cited in land-rights, poverty and service-delivery analysis; titled Amerindian lands cover a material share of national territory.

candidates.title: Education system — coverage, grants and feeding
candidates.description: Education-sector statistics and programmes: school infrastructure, Because We Care cash grant, uniform grant, school-feeding programme, and exam-fee support. Large and rising budget allocation financed in part by oil revenues.
candidates.notes: Primary human-capital and redistribution channel. Because We Care and school feeding are the most visible household-level education supports; hinterland and riverain schools receive targeted hot-meal and infrastructure attention.

candidates.title: Because We Care cash grant
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Education / Government of Guyana
candidates.description: Per-child cash grant paid to families of schoolchildren (public and private). Flagship education-linked transfer expanded under the oil-revenue budget.
candidates.notes: Lived cash-transfer node. Continuously cited as the main direct financial support reaching most school-age children; amount has been raised in successive budgets.

candidates.title: National School Feeding Programme
candidates.description: School-meal programme providing breakfast and hot meals, with particular emphasis on hinterland and riverain schools.
candidates.notes: Complementary in-kind support. Explicitly prioritises hinterland attendance and nutrition; also creates local catering livelihoods.

candidates.title: Health system — access and hinterland gaps
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Health / Bureau of Statistics
candidates.description: Public health-system statistics and outcomes. National indicators have improved but remain below regional averages; access and quality gaps are largest in the hinterland.
candidates.notes: Human-capital counterpart to education. Continuously cited for interior service-delivery challenges and for the need to convert oil revenues into better health outcomes outside the coastal strip.

candidates.title: Gold production and exports
candidates.publisher: Guyana Gold Board / Bureau of Statistics
candidates.description: Gold production and export statistics. Long-standing non-oil extractive sector, important in hinterland livelihoods and as a residual export earner.
candidates.notes: Primary non-oil extractive node. Continues to matter for hinterland employment and for export diversification even as oil dominates the aggregate accounts.

candidates.title: Rice and sugar — traditional agriculture
candidates.publisher: Bureau of Statistics / Guyana Sugar Corporation / GRDB
candidates.description: Rice and sugar production and export statistics. Historic coastal agricultural pillars that remain relevant for employment and rural livelihoods even as their relative economic weight has declined.
candidates.notes: Traditional coastal agro-export nodes. Continuously cited in non-oil sector analysis and in discussions of rural employment outside the oil and construction boom.

candidates.title: Bauxite production
candidates.description: Bauxite production and export statistics. Historic extractive sector, mainly in Region 10 and related areas; residual non-oil industrial activity.
candidates.notes: Legacy industrial-extractive node. Completes the non-oil primary-sector set alongside gold, rice and sugar.

proposed_edges.basis: Hinterland regions hold the large majority of the Indigenous population.
Georgetown sits inside Region 4, the demographic core.
Because We Care is a flagship education-linked cash grant.
School feeding is a core in-kind education and nutrition programme.
Education grants form a large component of the broader cash-transfer architecture.
Gold mining is a material livelihood activity in hinterland regions.
Rice and sugar remain components of non-oil output and employment.
Health-access gaps are most severe in the hinterland regions.
